At low to moderate JB-76 concentrations, the reaction rate in the presence of ascorbic acid is lower than the normal curve; but in the high JB-76 concentration region, the two curves gradually approach and tend toward the same plateau, indicating that under high concentrations of JB-76, the additional effect of ascorbic acid on the rate is weakened. This can explain why the two rate curves converge at high concentrations.
